purpose: Fifteenth expanded public source layer focused on source-reliability and process-boundary strategy for enzyme promiscuity and substrate engineering, whole-cell biotransformation, cell-free pathway reconstitution, cofactor regeneration, biocatalyst stability under solvent or loading stress, product inhibition and in situ product removal, biosensor or high-throughput screening lineage, and green-chemistry or sustainability critique of biocatalytic routes.

promotion_requirements: manual chemist, enzymologist, process, and data-lineage review

explicit substrate scope, enzyme lineage, engineering evidence, host or cell-free context, cofactor loop, stability boundary, product-removal method, screening provenance, or sustainability metric before proposal promotion
separate enzyme-promiscuity, whole-cell, cell-free cascade, cofactor-regeneration, process-stability, product-removal, screening-lineage, and green-chemistry critique policy

route-specific enzyme identity, assay lineage, host background, cofactor balance, solvent/loading tolerance, inhibition or equilibrium limitation, hit-screen reliability, downstream processing, and sustainability evidence review
biosecurity, host-engineering, screening false-positive, environmental, process-safety, waste, solvent, LCA, or scale-up review where relevant
safety_scope: records intentionally avoid quantities, operating conditions, expression instructions, and implementation protocols
v16 records are source-trust and process-boundary priors only and must not auto-close routes as stock, validated strain processes, or verified green-chemistry claims

families.name: Enzyme promiscuity, substrate walking, and active-site engineering policy
families.strategic_principle: Separate native enzyme precedent from promiscuous activity, engineered scope expansion, and assay lineage. A promiscuous hit is a source candidate, not proof of general substrate acceptance.

families.name: Whole-cell biotransformation, fermentation, pathway-host, and cell-factory boundaries
families.strategic_principle: Separate molecular enzyme logic from host uptake, toxicity, transport, competing metabolism, fermentation mode, and product export. Whole-cell records must carry host-context metadata.

families.name: Cell-free pathway reconstitution, enzyme cascade assembly, and substrate-channeling boundaries
families.strategic_principle: Separate target disconnection from enzyme order, intermediate channeling, cofactor balancing, enzyme ratio, and cell-free pathway provenance. Cell-free cascades are route programs, not single reaction templates.

families.name: NAD(P)H, flavin, ATP, SAM, electrochemical, and photochemical cofactor-regeneration policies
families.strategic_principle: Separate enzyme transformation from cofactor recycle loop, sacrificial substrate, electro/photochemical driver, and redox balance. The cofactor loop can be a route-defining strategic object.

families.name: Biocatalyst stability under solvent, temperature, substrate-loading, and inhibition stress
families.strategic_principle: Separate chemically plausible enzymatic disconnections from process viability under solvent, loading, temperature, inhibition, or catalyst-lifetime stress. Stability evidence gates process promotion.

families.name: Product inhibition, equilibrium limits, in situ product removal, extraction, membrane, and crystallization boundaries
families.strategic_principle: Separate molecular route feasibility from product inhibition, equilibrium, toxicity, and downstream removal. In situ removal is a strategic process boundary, not an incidental condition.

families.name: Biosensor, high-throughput screening, directed-evolution, and enzyme-hit lineage policy
families.strategic_principle: Separate route evidence from screening lineage, assay readout, false-positive risk, and evolution campaign provenance. A screened enzyme hit must carry how it was found and validated.

families.name: Green chemistry, circular-economy, LCA-style, waste, solvent, and sustainability critique for biocatalytic routes
families.strategic_principle: Separate biocatalysis as a method from evidence-backed sustainability. Lower temperature, aqueous media, or enzyme use is not automatically greener without solvent, waste, energy, feedstock, and scale evidence.

anchors.name: Promiscuous or engineered enzyme anchor with reviewed substrate scope, mutation lineage, and assay evidence
Whole-cell route anchor with reviewed host background, uptake/export, toxicity, and competing metabolism
Cell-free cascade anchor with reviewed enzyme order, intermediate channeling, cofactor balancing, and pathway provenance
Cofactor-regeneration anchor with reviewed recycle loop, redox or energy balance, and driver compatibility
Biocatalyst process-stability anchor with reviewed solvent, loading, inhibition, and catalyst-lifetime boundaries
In situ product-removal anchor with reviewed product inhibition, equilibrium, removal mode, and downstream compatibility
Screened enzyme-hit anchor with reviewed assay format, biosensor or droplet readout, and validation lineage
Sustainability critique anchor with reviewed solvent, waste, energy, feedstock, scale, and LCA-style evidence

disconnections.name: Target transformation to promiscuous enzyme hit plus scope-expansion and assay-lineage policy

break_bonds: assay hit to route evidence boundary
forward_logic: separate native enzyme precedent from promiscuous or engineered activity
track substrate similarity, assay format, and validation depth
flag routes where enzyme scope expansion is assumed from weak analog evidence
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Reward promiscuity records only when substrate similarity and assay lineage are explicit.

evidence.citation: Enzyme-promiscuity review frames promiscuity as an engine of evolutionary innovation rather than universal substrate scope.
Directed-evolution review discusses how protein catalysts are engineered and why lineage matters for catalytic claims.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit substrate similarity, enzyme lineage, assay format, and orthogonal validation

disconnections.name: Engineered substrate route to active-site variant plus substrate-walking policy

forward_logic: separate chemical substrate modification from enzyme-engineering evidence
track mutation set, selection objective, substrate series, and final validation
avoid promoting engineered variants without lineage and controls
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Use substrate-engineering records when route trust depends on how an enzyme variant was obtained.

evidence.citation: Natural-product enzyme-promiscuity review discusses harnessing promiscuity for synthesis across plants and microbes.
Enzyme-promiscuity review in carbohydrate-active enzymes describes applications and limits in biocatalysis.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit mutation, substrate-walking series, selection objective, and scale/validation status

disconnections.name: Whole-cell product to enzyme route plus host uptake/export, toxicity, and metabolism boundary

break_bonds: isolated enzyme route to whole-cell host boundary
forward_logic: separate enzyme transformation from host transport and metabolic background
track uptake, product export, host toxicity, and competing pathways
flag whole-cell records where isolated-enzyme evidence is being overextended
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Reward whole-cell routes only when host background and transport/toxicity constraints are explicit.

evidence.citation: Whole-cell biocatalysis review covers selective C-O functional-group introduction and modification in whole cells.
Whole-cell bioprocess review discusses permeability issues and membrane engineering in whole-cell processes.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit host, uptake/export, toxicity, strain lineage, and competing-metabolism policy

disconnections.name: Fermentation or cell-factory route to pathway host plus process-mode and product-export policy

forward_logic: separate molecular precursor logic from host pathway and process mode
track whether the route is batch fermentation, flow fermentation, simultaneous biocatalysis, or resting-cell transformation
carry export, downstream recovery, and host burden into route critique
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Use fermentation boundary records when host and process mode change route meaning.

evidence.citation: Flow-fermentation review discusses microsystems for whole-cell bioproduction processes.
Review on simultaneous fermentation and enzymatic biocatalysis describes combined process options.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit host, process mode, pathway context, product export, and downstream recovery

disconnections.name: Cell-free route to enzyme set plus pathway order, intermediate identity, and cofactor balance

break_bonds: single reaction to pathway program boundary
forward_logic: separate product synthesis into ordered enzyme modules and intermediates
track cofactor balance, enzyme compatibility, and intermediate accumulation
require pathway provenance before treating a cell-free route as source-backed
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Reward cell-free routes when enzyme order, intermediate identities, and cofactor balance are explicit.

evidence.citation: Cell-free pathway review covers tools and strategies for constructing cell-free enzyme pathways.
Synthetic-biology review describes design fundamentals for in vitro multi-enzyme reaction networks.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: high for explicit enzyme order, intermediate identities, cofactor balance, and pathway provenance

disconnections.name: Cell-free cascade to substrate-channeling or enzyme-scaffold policy

forward_logic: separate ordinary multi-enzyme mixture from scaffolded or channeling-dependent route
track intermediate stability, diffusion risk, and scaffold provenance
flag routes where channeling is invoked without evidence
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Use channeling records when intermediate handling, not only enzyme identity, defines feasibility.

evidence.citation: Substrate-channeling review covers enzyme complexes for biotechnological applications.
Multi-enzyme assembly review discusses strategies and perspectives for assembling multi-enzyme systems.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit scaffold, channeling rationale, labile intermediate, and enzyme-ratio policy

disconnections.name: Redox biocatalytic step to NAD(P)H recycle loop plus redox-balance policy

forward_logic: separate target redox step from cofactor-recycle method
track sacrificial substrate, hydrogenase, oxidase, dehydrogenase, or electrochemical driver
carry redox balance and byproduct burden into route ranking
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Reward redox biocatalysis only when cofactor recycle and redox balance are explicit.

evidence.citation: Redox-biocatalysis review compares nicotinamide cofactor-regeneration methods quantitatively.
Hydrogenase review discusses H2-driven NAD(P)+ cofactor regeneration.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: high for explicit cofactor identity, recycle module, redox balance, and byproduct policy

disconnections.name: Biocatalytic route to electrochemical, photochemical, or engineered cofactor-regeneration driver

forward_logic: separate enzyme transformation from electro/photochemical cofactor driver
track mediator, electrode, light, or engineered cofactor dependency
flag routes where energy input or mediator compatibility dominates feasibility
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Use electro/photo cofactor records when the driver is route-defining, not a generic condition.

evidence.citation: Electrochemical cofactor-regeneration review describes strategies for industrial biocatalysis reactors.
Cofactor-engineering review frames cofactor engineering as a driver of next-generation biomanufacturing.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit driver, mediator or energy source, cofactor identity, and enzyme-compatibility evidence

disconnections.name: Enzymatic route to solvent-tolerant biocatalyst plus nonaqueous process-stability policy

break_bonds: molecular route to solvent process boundary
forward_logic: separate substrate solubility needs from enzyme solvent tolerance
track solvent class, water activity, catalyst lifetime, and activity retention
avoid promoting solvent-dependent routes without stability evidence
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Reward solvent-stability records when solvent need and enzyme stability are both explicit.

evidence.citation: Solvent-tolerant enzyme review discusses adaptations and applications of extremophile enzymes.
Review on solvent-stable microbial lipases covers current understanding and biotechnological applications.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit solvent, enzyme stability, catalyst lifetime, and substrate-solubility rationale

disconnections.name: Biocatalytic route to high-loading or stressed process plus catalyst-stability and inhibition policy

forward_logic: separate enzyme activity proof from process-window evidence
track substrate loading, inhibition, temperature, lifetime, and engineering strategy
flag routes where scale-up assumes stability not shown in source evidence
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Use process-stability records when activity must survive loading, inhibition, temperature, or lifetime stress.

evidence.citation: Biocatalyst-stabilization review discusses strategies for stabilizing biocatalysts.
Protein-engineering review covers enzyme engineering for process applications.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit loading, inhibition, stability engineering, lifetime, and process window

disconnections.name: Biocatalytic product to in situ crystallization plus product-inhibition and equilibrium policy

forward_logic: separate molecular transformation from in situ crystallization or removal
track inhibition/equilibrium evidence, supersaturation, and downstream compatibility
avoid treating product removal as an incidental condition when it enables conversion
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Reward in situ crystallization records when product removal is necessary to overcome inhibition or equilibrium limits.

evidence.citation: ISPR crystallization review covers principles, design, and whole-cell biocatalysis applications.
In situ product crystallization review covers application of crystallization and related techniques in biocatalytic processes.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit inhibition/equilibrium limit, removal mode, downstream compatibility, and process evidence

disconnections.name: Biocatalytic route to extraction, membrane, adsorption, or phase-transfer product-removal policy

break_bonds: enzyme transformation to removal module boundary
forward_logic: separate target transformation from removal module design
track whether extraction, adsorption, membrane, or phase split relieves inhibition or shifts equilibrium
flag solvent and biocompatibility risks
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Use product-removal records when separation is a condition of feasibility rather than a downstream afterthought.

evidence.citation: ISPR crystallization review provides general context for integrating product recovery with whole-cell biocatalysis.
Biocatalytic-process crystallization review describes related in situ product-removal approaches.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit inhibition or equilibrium rationale, removal module, and enzyme compatibility

disconnections.name: Enzyme route to biosensor or high-throughput screen hit plus lineage and false-positive policy

break_bonds: screen hit to route evidence boundary
biosensor readout to product validation boundary
forward_logic: separate screen readout from chemical product validation
track assay format, reporter specificity, false-positive controls, and orthogonal validation
avoid treating a screening hit as a mature proposal source without lineage
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Reward screening-lineage records only when assay readout and product validation are explicit.

evidence.citation: Droplet-screening review covers advanced high-throughput strategies for enzyme engineering.
Transcription-factor biosensor review discusses high-throughput screening advances and applications.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit assay format, reporter specificity, hit lineage, and orthogonal validation

disconnections.name: Engineered route to directed-evolution library plus selection pressure and validation provenance

break_bonds: selection pressure to route objective boundary
forward_logic: separate final variant from library design and selection objective
track mutation lineage, assay pressure, and resynthesis or analytical validation
flag variants whose performance is tied to assay context
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Use directed-evolution provenance records when variant source quality is part of route trust.

evidence.citation: Metabolite-detection tool review covers high-throughput detection for metabolic engineering and directed-evolution applications.
Biosensor review discusses high-throughput library screening for metabolite production.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit parent, library, selection pressure, and orthogonal validation

disconnections.name: Biocatalytic route to sustainability claim plus solvent, energy, waste, feedstock, and comparator policy

forward_logic: separate biocatalysis label from evidence-backed sustainability
track solvent, waste, energy, feedstock, scale, and comparator route
flag routes where greenness is asserted without LCA-style evidence
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Reward sustainability claims only when metrics and comparator boundaries are explicit.

evidence.citation: Circular-economy review discusses enzymes, in vivo biocatalysis, and metabolic engineering for sustainability.
Critical evaluation of sustainable natural-product glycosylation compares biocatalytic and chemical approaches.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit solvent, waste, energy, feedstock, scale, and comparator evidence

disconnections.name: Biocatalytic process to LCA-style system boundary, scale, circularity, and waste policy

forward_logic: separate laboratory route plausibility from sustainability assessment boundary
track process scale, feedstock origin, solvent burden, catalyst lifetime, and waste stream
require comparator and system boundary before ranking as greener
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Use LCA-boundary records when the strategic decision is route critique, not bond disconnection.

evidence.citation: Industrial biocatalysis review discusses acceleration of biocatalysis implementation in industry.
Circular-economy review frames enzyme and in vivo biocatalysis in sustainability contexts.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit system boundary, scale, waste/solvent metric, and comparator process

source_notes.summary: The v16 expansion promotes source-reliability and process-boundary backlog families covering enzyme promiscuity, whole-cell context, cell-free cascades, cofactor regeneration, process stability, product removal, screening lineage, and sustainability critique.

V16 records are advisory. Promotion requires explicit source lineage, host or process boundary, cofactor/stability/removal evidence where relevant, and sustainability or screening claims must be supported by comparator and validation metadata.
